bib.title: Mesh-TensorFlow: Deep Learning for Supercomputers
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2018 (32nd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: How can model-parallel (and mixed data/model-parallel) training be specified simply enough to train much larger Transformers on TPU meshes?
hypothesis: Splitting arbitrary named tensor dimensions across a multi-dimensional processor mesh removes the memory and small-batch limits of pure data-parallelism, and scaling model size this way improves quality.
contributions: Mesh-TensorFlow, a language for specifying distributed tensor computations as named tensor dimensions mapped to named mesh dimensions via a computation layout, compiled to SPMD with collectives
Analysis of communication, computation and memory costs for data-, model- and mixed layouts (Table 1)
A model-parallel Transformer (split vocab, d_ff, heads) trained up to 4.9B parameters on 512 TPUv2 cores with new state-of-the-art WMT14 En-Fr and One Billion Word results

method.summary: A Python library where tensors carry named dimensions and a layout maps tensor dimensions to mesh dimensions; it lowers to SPMD TensorFlow for TPUs. Used to train Transformers whose vocab, d_ff and heads dimensions are split over one mesh axis and batch over the other.
method.task: distributed training framework; LM and machine translation with Transformers

results.claim: Pure data-parallel layout allreduces about 2*d_io*d_h values per processor (the parameter count), independent of batch size.
Pure model-parallel layout allreduces 2*b*d_io values per processor; mixed data+model layout allreduces 2*b*d_io/r + 2*d_io*d_h/c.
results.setup: Two fully-connected layers on n processors / r x c mesh, Sec 8.2-8.3

results.claim: In a 2-D data+model mesh, processor count can grow quadratically while batch and layer size grow only linearly at constant efficiency (cubically in a 3-D mesh).

limits: Optimizer, learning rate, schedule, dropout, precision, layer counts and tokenizer are not given; deferred to tensor2tensor.
Single runs, no variance; no compute-optimal or data-scaling analysis, scaling is in parameters only with fixed data epochs.
Perplexity gains flatten at the top (24.1 to 24.0); En-De quality drops at 2.89B, blamed on small data.
Layout search is manual; automated layout search listed as future work.
Only TPU SPMD and multi-CPU/GPU MIMD implemented; SPMD on GPU clusters is future work.
Cost accounting is wall-clock and PFLOP/s only; no total FLOPs, energy or dollar cost.

terms.definition: an n-dimensional array of such processors; only a naming abstraction and does not imply a physical network topology
A global computation layout is a partial map from tensor-dimension to mesh-dimension
